question.text: A bag is gently dropped on a conveyor belt moving at a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The coefficient of friction between the conveyor belt and bag is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn></math> Initially, the bag slips on the belt before it stops due to friction. The distance travelled by the bag on the belt during slipping motion is : [Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
When the bag is dropped on the conveyor belt, the acceleration of the bag will be a=μg=4 m s-2

The bag will stop moving on the conveyor when the velocity of the bag and the velocity of the conveyor becomes equal.

u=0, v=2 m s-1

Using the equation of motion for constant acceleration,

v2=u2+2as

⇒s=0.5 m
